issues.legal_issue: Luxury tax on a multi-apartment residential building is computed by aggregating the qualifying area held by each owner, rather than by treating every apartment as a separate unit regardless of ownership.
material_facts: The residential building was completed after the date from which the luxury-tax charge applied and contained 13 apartments.
The respondent owned all 13 apartments, and the total area of the apartments exceeded the statutory threshold, although each apartment individually was below it.
The revenue authority assessed tax by combining the areas of all the apartments.
The lower courts treated the apartments separately for the assessment.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, and the matter was remanded for the tax to be computed according to ownership: areas of apartments retained by one owner are aggregated, while apartments owned by different persons are assessed separately. A person owning multiple apartments is assessed on their combined area.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5A of the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975 is the charging provision and begins with a non-obstante clause. It must be read with the definitions of “building” and “residential building” in Sections 2(e) and 2(l), and the definition of “plinth area” and its proviso in Section 2(k), including Explanation II to Section 2(e). The provisions are to be harmoniously and purposively construed: separate ownership calls for separate computation, while area held by one owner is aggregated. Joint meeting of construction costs is not confined to contributions made before construction; a purchaser may share that cost through the purchase price. The Court relied on State of T.N. v. Kodaikanal Motor Union (P) Ltd., K.P. Varghese v. ITO, Luke v. IRC, and Keshavji Ravji and Co. v. CIT for purposive interpretation, including avoiding absurd results when a literal reading of a taxation provision would defeat its object.

rule.if: tax_assessment_appeal and residential_multi_unit_building and qualifying_completion_timing and ownership_pattern_established and an_owner_group_area_meets_threshold

predicates.tax_assessment_appeal: The proceeding challenges an assessment of luxury tax on a residential building.
predicates.residential_multi_unit_building: The building contains more than one residential apartment or flat.
predicates.qualifying_completion_timing: The building was completed during the period in which the luxury-tax charge applies.
predicates.ownership_pattern_established: The apartments or flats held by each owner can be identified.
predicates.an_owner_group_area_meets_threshold: The combined area of the qualifying apartments or flats held by at least one owner reaches the applicable tax threshold.

issues.definition: When a qualifying multi-apartment residential building is the subject of a tax-assessment appeal, the relevant ownership pattern is established, and an owner’s combined area reaches the threshold, the tax is computed by aggregating the units held by each owner.
